{{Short description|Dutch physicist}}
'''Erik Petrus Antonius Maria Bakkers''' (born 18 December 1972, in [[Kaatsheuvel]]) is a professor at the physics departments of both the [[Eindhoven University of Technology|Eindhoven]] and [[Delft University of Technology|Delft]] Universities of Technology. His research concentrates on the growth and properties of semiconducting nanowires, the use of wires for solar cells, thermoelectric devices, and [[quantum computation]]. He received his PhD from the [[Utrecht University]]  with the thesis [http://dspace.library.uu.nl/bitstream/handle/1874/734/full.pdf;jsessionid=7933157C04DB3B208A4143FC18271AE6?sequence=1 "Charge transfer between semiconductor nanocrystals and a metal"], which was focused on charge transfer between [[quantum dot]]s. He worked at [[Philips]] Research labs in [[Eindhoven]] for 9 years before moving back to academia. Bakkers received the Technical Review award from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] in 2007,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www2.technologyreview.com/tr35/profile.aspx?trid=602 | title=Erik Bakkers, 34 | work=MIT Technology Review | date=2007 | accessdate=29 June 2015 | archive-date=6 September 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906181249/http://www2.technologyreview.com/tr35/profile.aspx?trid=602 | url-status=dead }}</ref> a VICI award in 2010,  and the Science AAAS Newcomb Cleveland Prize in 2013.

Bakkers was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://knaw.nl/en/members/members/16608 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200502084334/https://knaw.nl/en/members/members/16608 |title=Erik Bakkers |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=2 May 2020}}</ref>
